rationale: I read the actual Isaac Lab v1 RGB-distillation paragraph: partial versus privileged inputs can produce a performance drop, particularly with camera occlusion. It does not establish this illustration coefficients, numeric discrepancy or a universal no-training-budget error floor. The unsupported empirical interpretation is corrected.

inventory.text: The neighboring teacher/student explanation distinguishes privileged simulator state from deployable proprioceptive/history inputs.
Isaac Lab calls the teacher/student difference an information gap due to input mismatch and discusses reconstruction under camera occlusion.
The 24-cell terrain, LCG seeds 123456789 and 987654321, sigma-3 blur, noise/occlusion coefficients, degradation range 0–1 and default 0.15 are authored construction.
The specified local reconstruction, MAE, occlusion and 2.2*MAE normalized action divergence are derived from degradation, increasing by construction rather than reported distillation results.
The actual teacher mount starts at degradation 0.15 and Reset returns the original input/reconstruction markup, MAE 0.01 m, discrepancy 0.02 and 3/24 occluded channels.
